summary.text: Mike Ezell is the U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 4th Congressional District, in office since 2023, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results. A Gulf Coast native, he was a law enforcement officer for more than forty years, most recently as sheriff of Jackson County, before winning the seat in 2022 by defeating incumbent Steven Palazzo in a Republican primary runoff. He chairs the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Ezell is a native of the Mississippi Gulf Coast who lives in Pascagoula and graduated from Pascagoula High School in 1977. He earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice from the University of Southern Mississippi in 1997, and according to his official biography he also graduated from the Mississippi Law Enforcement Training Academy and the FBI National Academy.
He worked in law enforcement for more than forty years, most recently as sheriff of Jackson County.

Ezell placed second in the June 7, 2022 Republican primary for the 4th District behind incumbent Steven Palazzo, then won the June 28 runoff, 53.8% to 46.2%. He won the November 8, 2022 general election with 73.3% of the vote, defeating Democrat Johnny DuPree and Libertarian Alden Johnson, and took office in 2023.

In Congress, Ezell serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, chairing its Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee, and on the Natural Resources Committee, where he is vice chairman of the Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife and Fisheries.
He won the March 10, 2026 Republican primary over Sawyer Walters, 84.1% to 15.9%.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Suzette, live in Pascagoula and attend First Baptist Church of Pascagoula.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 61.1% of the vote to Jeffrey Hulum III's 35.8% and Carl Boyanton's 3.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
